nodes.label: Cross-platform CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Gate changes on formatting, warning-free clippy, tests, Docker configuration, image construction, and a daemon smoke test on supported platforms.

nodes.label: Daemon Image Smoke Test
nodes.rationale: Use a shell-wrapped sleep stand-in so daemon-appended permission flags are harmless while the test verifies session creation settles to waiting.

nodes.label: Release Please Automation
nodes.rationale: Maintain one release PR from Conventional Commits and let its merge create the version tag and GitHub Release.

nodes.label: GitHub App Release Authentication
nodes.rationale: The default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot trigger required CI on the release PR, so a narrowly permissioned GitHub App token performs writes.

nodes.label: Release Branch Cargo.lock Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Generic TOML updaters cannot target Cargo.lock package entries, so the workflow refreshes and conditionally commits the lockfile on the release branch.

nodes.label: Tiered Release Policy
nodes.rationale: Patch releases merge when checks pass, minor releases undergo a soak, and major releases require human review.

nodes.label: Minor Release Soak Gate
nodes.rationale: Merge minor release PRs only after the configured age and all required checks pass, while allowing a release:hold veto and manual fast-track.

nodes.label: Release Asset Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Trigger from the Release published event to avoid colliding with release-please ownership of the tag and GitHub Release.

nodes.label: Cross-platform Binary Tarballs
nodes.rationale: Package both baude and bauded so tarball or mise installs can satisfy automatic daemon discovery.

nodes.label: Session Attention Core Value
nodes.rationale: Users should see which Claude Code session needs them next and act from either terminal or phone.

nodes.label: VPN-only Single-user Security Model
nodes.rationale: The self-hosted single-user service relies on binding a Tailscale or VPN interface instead of adding an application authentication layer.

nodes.label: First-party Claude Data Preference
nodes.rationale: Status-line JSON and hooks provide more accurate state and unlock PR, effort, and activity information without inference.

nodes.label: Deferred Human UAT Set
nodes.rationale: The remaining gaps are visual, device, and live-Claude observations rather than known code or integration gaps.

nodes.label: Spawn Permission Mode Fallback
nodes.rationale: Use spawn intent when transcript permission mode is unavailable, while preserving transcript data as authoritative when present.

nodes.label: Prompt Mode Command Conflict Resolution
nodes.rationale: An explicit prompt-mode opt-in should strip a conflicting skip-permissions flag from the base command and warn, avoiding a half-configured MCP state.

nodes.label: Tiered Auto-release Gating Design
nodes.rationale: Layer patch auto-merge, a configurable minor soak, and manual major approval on top of release-please because release-please does not provide those gates itself.

nodes.label: Release Event Build Handoff
nodes.rationale: release-please owns tag and Release creation; the existing build subscribes to release publication and only uploads assets, preventing a double-release collision.

nodes.label: Three-state Session Status
nodes.rationale: Separate calm completed turns from urgent needs-input states so only sessions genuinely blocked on the user demand attention.

nodes.label: Idle Kind Classifier
nodes.rationale: Refine only the existing idle bucket based on the newest Stop or Notification event without changing the tested Hook > SessionFile > Silence precedence engine.

nodes.label: Fail-safe Needs-input Classification
nodes.rationale: Unknown idle state remains needs-input because a false alert is safer than hiding a session blocked on the user.

nodes.label: Completed Notification Policy
nodes.rationale: Emit one gentler finished notification on Working-to-Completed while preserving urgent input and permission notifications.

nodes.label: Integration-clean v0.7 Audit
nodes.rationale: All requirements are code-complete and all cross-phase seams are wired; remaining debt consists of human verification and documented limitations.

nodes.label: Schema 2 Bridge Writer
nodes.rationale: Factor bridge construction into build_bridge for stdin-free tests while retaining best-effort capture and Value-based compatibility.

nodes.label: Additive ClaudeMeta Reader
nodes.rationale: Optional Value accessors support old and future bridge schemas without schema branches; bridge model wins only when present.

nodes.label: Conditional Metadata Rows
nodes.rationale: Render effort, thinking, and PR only when present; keep vim mode captured but hidden and leave remote parity out of scope.

nodes.label: In-file Analog Extension Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each Phase 1 change should mirror an exact pattern already present in the same target file rather than introduce a foreign abstraction.

nodes.label: Value-accessor Compatibility Pattern
nodes.rationale: serde_json::Value accessors, object guards, and optional fields make unknown, absent, and wrong-type data non-fatal without schema-specific branches.

nodes.label: Additive Bridge Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Keep schema informational and parse all bridge fields optionally so stale files self-heal and readers tolerate both older and future writers.

nodes.label: Authoritative Status-Line Bridge
nodes.rationale: The bridge is the authoritative payload source while additive optional fields and untyped Value accessors preserve compatibility with older readers.

nodes.label: Idempotent Hook Settings Merge
nodes.rationale: The hook command string doubles as the sentinel, preventing duplicate entries while preserving user statusLine, hooks, and sibling settings.

nodes.label: State Source Precedence
nodes.rationale: Fresh hook events are prepended as the highest-precedence state source while the session-file and silence branches remain unchanged to avoid a v0.6.1 regression.

nodes.label: Capture but Render Lightly
nodes.rationale: State source and last tool are exposed as minimal overlay rows while richer activity presentation is deferred to Phase 3.

nodes.label: Untyped Value Schema-Drift Discipline
nodes.rationale: Claude-originated JSON is read through untyped Value accessors so absent, renamed, malformed, or wrong-type fields degrade safely instead of breaking deserialization.

nodes.label: Never-Block Hook Posture
nodes.rationale: The hook command exits zero unconditionally and treats transport as best-effort because non-zero or blocking hooks interfere with Claude turns.

nodes.label: Bounded Hook POST with File Fallback
nodes.norm_label: bounded hook post with file fallback

nodes.label: Single-Source Activity Ring
nodes.rationale: ClaudeMeta owns one bounded ring that both the local TUI and daemon consume, avoiding a mirrored buffer and synchronization drift.

nodes.label: GET-Then-SSE Backfill
nodes.rationale: The client opens SSE into a temporary buffer before fetching history, then drains buffered events so no activity falls into the snapshot/live race window.

nodes.label: Snapshot-to-Tail Buffering
nodes.rationale: Connect the activity SSE before loading the REST snapshot, buffer arrivals, then drain them so events are not lost at the snapshot/live boundary.

nodes.label: Activity Feed XSS Escaping
nodes.rationale: Every event-origin string is escaped before innerHTML interpolation because tool and notification text is untrusted display data.

nodes.label: Render Last N Activity Events
nodes.rationale: Anchor the newest events at the bottom and defer paging older events to the REST endpoint instead of adding modal scroll state in the first cut.

nodes.label: Standalone Activity SSE Channel
nodes.rationale: Keep activity transport independent from chat streaming so clients can subscribe to either channel and reuse the proven file-tail pattern.

nodes.label: Offset File Tail Pattern
nodes.rationale: Reuse complete-lines-only offset tracking and truncation reset while changing only the per-line parser for hook events.

nodes.label: Activity Surface Pattern Reuse
nodes.rationale: The browser strip mirrors openChat and the terminal overlay mirrors Modal::Info, minimizing new mechanisms.

nodes.label: EventTail Parser Separation
nodes.rationale: Transcript Tail parses ChatMessage records, so activity streaming requires a distinct parser for HookEvent JSONL despite sharing offset machinery.

nodes.label: Activity Validation Split
nodes.rationale: Rust data and API behavior is automated, while browser and terminal rendering remain manual because no suitable JS or TUI interaction harness exists.

nodes.label: MCP Config Seeding Plan
nodes.rationale: Prompt mode seeds a current-executable stdio MCP registration while preserving existing user MCP servers and never aborting spawn on seed failure.

nodes.label: Non-Clobbering MCP Merge
nodes.rationale: A pure merge updates only mcpServers.baude so sibling servers and unrelated top-level configuration survive.

nodes.label: MCP Contract UAT Gate
nodes.rationale: The exact Claude Code permission-tool framing, request fields, and accepted result envelope were not officially specified end to end, so live raw-frame verification gates shipping prompt mode.

nodes.label: Lean Permission Push
nodes.rationale: Push notifications carry only a generic permission marker and session identity; sensitive tool details are fetched from the daemon API.

nodes.label: Single-Call Permission Decision Semantics
nodes.rationale: Deny posts a permission decision for one tool invocation and must not interrupt or terminate the broader Claude session.

nodes.label: Deny on Timeout
nodes.rationale: A missing phone decision must fail closed after a bounded wait; the permission bridge never auto-allows.

nodes.label: Core Transform and Binary IO Split
nodes.rationale: Keep JSON-RPC transformations pure and testable in baude-core while stdin and HTTP remain in each executable, following dispatch_hook.
nodes.norm_label: core transform and binary io split

nodes.label: Await Outside Manager Lock
nodes.rationale: Mutate pending state under the manager lock but release it before waiting for a human so one permission does not stall all sessions.

nodes.label: MCP Contract Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: Official documentation establishes MCP tool naming and registration but not the complete request fields, response wrapping, or framing for the installed CLI, requiring a live contract test.

nodes.label: No New Permission Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Existing ureq, serde_json, axum, and tokio cover the one-tool bridge and daemon API, avoiding a heavy MCP SDK dependency.

nodes.label: Live MCP Permission Wire Contract
nodes.rationale: A live Claude CLI probe was required because no complete official example established the permission-prompt-tool wire shape.

nodes.label: Newline-Delimited JSON MCP Framing
nodes.rationale: Claude Code accepts newline-delimited JSON on MCP stdout and silently drops Content-Length-framed output.

nodes.label: Application JSON Permission Registration Fix
nodes.rationale: Posting text/plain caused the daemon JSON extractor to return 415 and made prompt mode silently deny every tool.

nodes.label: Live Permission Contract Gate
nodes.rationale: The MCP contract and browser behavior remain manual because the wire contract lacked an authoritative example and the vanilla-JS PWA has no test runner.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Permission Policy
nodes.rationale: Timeouts, missing daemons, invalid decisions, and transport failures deny rather than permit tool execution.

nodes.label: XSS-Escaped Permission Card
nodes.rationale: Tool input is escaped before rendering so untrusted input cannot break layout or inject markup.

nodes.label: Live Wire Schema Drift
nodes.rationale: Bundled SDK types disagreed with observed event names and payload fields, so the driver must target pinned live wire behavior.

nodes.label: Server API Over Plugin Decision
nodes.rationale: The documented permission.ask hook never fires in opencode 1.18.16, while a plugin observer would still need the same HTTP endpoint and add a seeded artifact.

nodes.label: Plugin Spike HTTP Fallback Approval Proof
nodes.norm_label: plugin spike http fallback approval proof

nodes.label: Node ESM Spike Stack
nodes.rationale: External HTTP and JavaScript surfaces are probed with dependency-free Node scripts for speed despite the main repository being Rust.

nodes.label: Prove Deferral Before Outcome
nodes.rationale: Approval tests must show that a side effect does not occur while the decision is held, not merely that the final outcome is correct.

nodes.label: Backend Seam and Session Lifecycle Work
nodes.norm_label: backend seam and session lifecycle work

nodes.label: Input Modal Polish and v0.9 Release
nodes.norm_label: input modal polish and v0.9 release

nodes.label: Hard-Separated Workspaces
nodes.rationale: Workspace-specific state and backend binding prevent Claude and opencode sessions from mixing during restore or daemon use.

nodes.label: Tailnet Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: bauded shares the Tailscale sidecar network namespace and publishes no host ports, making the VPN the access-control boundary.

nodes.label: Tailnet Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: Nothing is published to the host and the daemon has no authentication layer because the tailnet is the security boundary.

nodes.label: Hook-Driven Status Events
nodes.rationale: Claude Code hooks replace the approximate PTY-silence heuristic with authoritative event-driven session state.

nodes.label: File-Tail Event Transport
nodes.rationale: File-tail transport matches the existing meta reader patterns and avoids a new local network bind.

nodes.label: BAUDE Permission Mode
nodes.rationale: The skip default preserves unattended behavior, while prompt mode enables phone approval but can block unattended sessions.

nodes.label: Inline Review Comments
nodes.rationale: Contextual diff comments reuse the existing message-injection and busy-session queue path, making review feedback inexpensive to add.

nodes.label: Diff Size Pagination
nodes.rationale: Diffs should be paginated by file so a phone is not sent a very large unified diff at once.

nodes.label: Prepared-Not-Fired Safety Gate
nodes.rationale: Scheduled and webhook jobs should require explicit autonomous opt-in before firing potentially destructive prompts unattended.

nodes.label: Autonomy Budget Cap
nodes.rationale: Parallel races and scheduled sessions multiply spend, so aggregate cost and a per-day cap should constrain autonomy.

nodes.label: Stable-Order Grouping
nodes.rationale: Grouping remains opt-in and preserves order within groups because stable sidebar order prevents busy-session thrashing.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Safety Gate
nodes.rationale: Repository bootstrap scripts execute arbitrary code and therefore require explicit opt-in for trusted repositories.

nodes.label: Message-Posting Model
nodes.rationale: Structured message posting avoids remote terminal rendering, multi-client resize problems, and an xterm.js dependency.

nodes.label: Authentication Test Flakiness
nodes.rationale: The failure repeats every third CI run because three 10-second fake-timer advances reach the mock token's fixed 30-second expiry boundary.

nodes.label: Pin Token Expiry to Fake Clock
nodes.norm_label: pin token expiry to fake clock
